sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: setlist.fm: on a page long enough to scroll, the toolbar above our table (the action button and ☰ SAED) no longer disappears under a dark bar as soon as it sticks to the top. The backdrop meant to sit behind it lay over our whole section, in the colour of setlist.fm's dark page. Discogs and archive.org use the same rule now; MusicBrainz and the Springsteen sites are unchanged.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: discogs.com, archive.org and setlist.fm: after a press only the table view shows; the site's own page no longer sits under our tables. The switch of WIP.1 (☰ SAED → View → "📄 Show the original page", Ctrl+M P, "▦ Back to the tables") shows the site's own page again, live and fully working, with a "Live" note on top, and hides our section; back again, the tables are as you left them. The site's header stays only where it sits above our section (a Discogs master, release, artist or label page); where our section comes first (archive.org, setlist.fm, Discogs' search, submissions and user pages) the header hides with the page, and so does the footer. Before a press nothing changes. The site's page stays laid out while hidden, so its own scripts keep working: archive.org's player and pictures are still there after the switch.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: MusicBrainz pages: switch between the tables and the original page, and back, as often as you like, without a reload. After a "Show all …" press, ☰ SAED → View → "📄 Show the original page" (or Ctrl+M, then P) shows the page as it was just before the press: MusicBrainz's own list with its pages, its tracklist, its sidebar. A "▦ Back to the tables" button bottom right (or Ctrl+M P again) brings the tables back as you left them: the same rows, the filter you typed, the sort, and where you had scrolled. The original page is a copy taken at the press, so it switches at once and costs no request; a note on it says so, since MusicBrainz's own buttons in it (rating stars, "Load all tracks", the credits toggle) may not respond. Esc never switches. A load from disk takes the copy too. Every render opens on the tables; the choice is not remembered. With majkinetor's scripts, the button stacks with his corner launchers, and while the original page shows his launchers, keys and player behave as on a page without our tables. Like Event Horizon's V (org/majkinetor.org, "Switch between SAED's view and the original page (EH's V)"; approved mockup https://claude.ai/artifact/9wsKwn3kSr7LvhBkJVcijf).
